problem: Does the edge-five carrier realize a five-sheeted period cover of the existing global wiring while retaining all 80 physical P and E cell identities?
conjecture: The larger window's P/E occurrences separate the five sheets over every source cell fibre for at least one index-five sublattice of the existing period lattice.
rivals: The window has five occurrences per P/E base fibre but their period coordinates cannot simultaneously separate all sheets
The native bulk fails even to project incidence-preservingly to the existing candidate
source: The rank-three period lattice and exact edge transports already declared by sulfur-32-wiring.mjs. No new physical closure authority is inferred.
construction: Project every physical window cell and port by exact period translation. Enumerate kernels of all normalized nonzero F5 covectors on the three period generators. Lift every source edge to five sheets using its existing translation cocycle; compute components only after assembling the complete graph.
completeness: Every index-five subgroup of Z^3 is the kernel of a nonzero homomorphism to Z/5. Covectors have the same kernel exactly when they differ by a nonzero scalar. There are (125-1)/4=31 kernels.
riskyTests: Every native bulk edge projects to a lifted edge in every cover
Each global cover has 80 P, N and E fibres and 320 nonbranching same-axis wires
At least one cover separates all 80 P and all 80 E physical cells
noncollapse: Retain physical occurrence identities and cover sheet coordinates even when the projected labels coincide. Distinct physical P cells with the same lifted cell are a failure, not an authorized payload identification.
stop: If no cover separates the window, reject this realization branch. Do not select a cover, exchange cells, or reinterpret 80 named physical fibres to force a realization.
